The People’s Review of Prevent gives a voice to the people most impacted by the Prevent Duty. This review, launched in February 2022, is organised and supported by a wider range of people and organisations. It is an alternative to the review conducted for the government by William Shawcross. Where Shawcross has dismissed criticisms of Prevent, this report reviews the evidence about the operation of Prevent and the harms that it causes to individuals and communities. The report shows that Prevent is discriminatory in its impact on Muslim communities. It is directed primarily at children and young people who make up around half of all referrals. This includes children at nursery and primary schools.

Prevent Watch is a community led initiative which supports people impacted by Prevent. Established in September 2014, it has supported hundreds of cases. Its case studies "show a huge failing of the Prevent Duty. It provides a free helpline with dedicated case workers to support people impacted by the Prevent Duty. It provides access to lawyers, media, research and much more. The Prevent Duty is championed by the government as an effective strategy to prevent terrorism, however, evidence suggests this is having an adverse effect on communities. Thousands of Prevent referrals are made each year but very few of them lead to any intervention."

Islam 21c is a media site giving an Islamic perspective on current affairs. Islam21c began as a project launched in 2006 and later owned by Fig and Olive Media. It was set up to provide a digital representation for the Muslim community in Britain to express, share and educate the UK and International community of their rich and diverse culture as British Muslims through various forms of art including film, poetry, literature, and digital design. We work with many aspiring and talented British Muslim men and women, to help them explore and create their cultural expressions through the various art forms via our team of specialists and share their work with the digital world. The company also trains and develops young visionaries in particular to become specialists in their fields to then further inspire and develop others to do the same.

Suhaiymah Manzoor-Khan is a writer, poet and educator disrupting understandings of history, race, knowledge and violence. She works to equip herself and others with the tools and faith to resist the unliveable conditions we find ourselves in, and work towards another reality. Suhaiymah is co-author of A Fly Girl’s Guide to University (Verve Poetry Press, 2019), author of Postcolonial Banter (Verve Poetry Press, 2019), and Tangled in Terror: Uprooting Islamophobia (Pluto Press, forthcoming 2022), as well as host of the Breaking Binaries podcast (currently on hiatus). She has essays in I Refuse To Condemn (Manchester University Press, 2020) and Cut From The Same Cloth? (Unbound, 2021) and has written for The Guardian, Independent, Al-Jazeera, and gal-dem.
